audit.title: Automation Best Practices

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Each section leads with the recommendation, e.g. "For registration on Mainnet, you need ERC-677 LINK." Sections stand alone with no back-references. Minor: "Use the Forwarder" opens on a conditional rather than the core rule.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Sections are short and coherent (median 46 words), but the measured **1 level skip** (H1 directly to H3, no H2) flattens the hierarchy, and **0 bullets / 0 tables** means the nine best practices aren't presented as an extractable list. A summary bullet list or "Do/Don't" table would improve chunk selection.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only 4 numerals per 1k words, **0 with units**, and vague quantifier "many token bridges." No version numbers (v1/v2 mentioned but no exact release), no latency/limit figures for the "flickering" latency claim.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Mostly internal links (6 of 7); the sole external link is PegSwap. **0 links to primary sources** and 1 opaque link ("convert Chainlink tokens...") reduce attributability. ERC-677 and ERC-20 are named but not linked to the token standard.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Middling. "Flickering" is described but not crisply defined in one liftable sentence; no canonical one-line definitions for `Forwarder`, `Registry`, or `StreamsLookup`.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak per measured facts: **0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified**. Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read, but the JSON-LD/canonical absence is confirmed.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: **0 fenced code blocks.** Advice like "add a setter function with permissions" and "revalidate the conditions in `checkUpkeep`" is exactly where a short Solidity snippet would make the page agent-runnable.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the lifecycle (versioning, config, security, testing, tokens) but headings are imperative/concept-titled, not symptom-phrased. Missing the retrieval-winning question forms: "Why isn't my upkeep being performed?", "How do I restrict performUpkeep?"

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Terminology (`Forwarder`, `Registry`, `checkUpkeep`, `performUpkeep`) is consistent and unambiguous.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-written best-practices guide for Chainlink Automation with nine short, coherent sections that each open with actionable advice — genuinely strong on clarity and answer-first phrasing. Its biggest GEO weaknesses are mechanical and fixable: no code snippets, near-zero concrete specifics (4 numerals, no units, vague "many"), a missing H2 layer (H1→H3 skip), and absent structured metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates). The headings are concept/imperative-titled rather than symptom-phrased, so the page will lose retrieval on the exact queries developers type ("why is my upkeep not performing"). Solid prose held back from citation by thin specifics and no machine-readable envelope.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased section headings/anchors
recommendations.where: "Avoid 'flickering' custom logic upkeeps" and "Use the Forwarder"
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled headings miss how devs query failures.
recommendations.change: Add question sub-anchors or reword, e.g. "Why isn't my upkeep being performed? (avoid flickering)" and "How do I restrict `performUpkeep` to the Forwarder?"
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom, not concept name; question-phrased headings win retrieval body text loses.

recommendations.title: Add a top-of-page summary list of the practices
recommendations.issue: 9 practices exist only as prose sections; 0 bullets, 0 tables.
recommendations.change: Insert a bulleted checklist (one line per practice) or a "Practice / Why it matters" table so an engine can lift the full set as one chunk.
recommendations.why: Bulleted/tabular decision factors let engines extract reasons and build justified answers.

recommendations.title: Fix the heading hierarchy
recommendations.where: All sections use H3 under the H1.
recommendations.change: Promote the nine best-practice sections to H2.
recommendations.why: Correct hierarchy improves RAG chunk boundaries and section retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema, canonical URL, and last-updated date
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about` (Chainlink Automation), plus a `<link rel="canonical">` and a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parse-ability and trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Add short Solidity snippets for the two actionable practices
recommendations.where: "Use the Forwarder" and "Automation v1 upkeep revalidation"
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks; advice is prose-only ("add a setter function with permissions").
recommendations.change: Add a labeled `solidity` snippet showing a mutable `forwarder` variable with an `onlyOwner` setter and a `require(msg.sender == forwarder)` guard; and a `checkUpkeep`-revalidation block inside `performUpkeep`.
recommendations.why: Complete, copy-pasteable snippets are directly liftable by coding agents completing these exact tasks.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers and add concrete specifics
recommendations.where: "Many token bridges give you ERC-20 LINK"; "latency between observing... consensus"
recommendations.change: Name the token standards with links, and quantify where possible (e.g. block-confirmation window, DON check cadence) or state the exact versions where "latest" applies.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Add primary-source and standard links; fix opaque link text
recommendations.where: "Using ERC-677 tokens" and the PegSwap link
recommendations.change: Link "ERC-677" and "ERC-20" to their EIP specs and give the PegSwap link descriptive text ("convert ERC-20 LINK to ERC-677 via PegSwap").
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a one-line canonical definition of "flickering"
recommendations.issue: Behavior is described diffusely, not defined.
recommendations.change: Lead with: "A 'flickering' upkeep is one whose `checkUpkeep` rapidly alternates between true and false, risking non-execution."
recommendations.why: A crisp, self-contained definition is verbatim-liftable.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier: "Many token bridges give you ERC-20 LINK tokens" — replace with named bridges/standards.
Opaque link text on the PegSwap conversion link.
Undated content (no visible last-updated), which reads as potentially stale to engines.
No walls of text, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff — clean on those axes.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templates and a freshness cadence (dateModified) are best solved at the docs-platform level, not per-page.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served content; pass raw `<head>` to the CLI for a definitive metadata read.
